newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's WAPET oil group cuts 210 jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's WAPET oil group cuts 210 jobs.

text.p: The West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) oil consortium said on Monday it would cut 210 jobs out of 566 as part of a resutructuring to reduce operating costs in the face of declining oil production.
The proposed Gorgon gas project offshore of Western Australia is excluded from the restructuring, Malcom Sandman, legal respresentative for Wapet, told Reuters.

Sandman said the measure was designed to improve the return on investment for WAPET partners Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh.
The majority of the job cuts will occur in WAPET's Perth headquarters although the main oil producing assets of Barrow and Thevenard islands also will be affected, Sandman said.
Combined oil production from the two fields is projected to decline to about 30,000 barrels a day next year, from 60,000 barrels a day in 1995, he said.

Wapet's Dongara gas fields operations and the Wang pipeline project, which are located in the North Perth Basin region of Western Australia, will be less affected as these assets are up for sale, Sandman said.
The overall aim of the restructuring is to reduce operating costs by about 25 percent starting next year, Sandman said.
total expenditures by the partners in 1995 totaled A$275 million, excluding capital costs, Sandman said.
"The reorganisation is due to a projected reduction in the return on investment by the joint venture participants over the next couple of years, due to declining oil production," he said.

Sandman also said no decision has been made over a proposal to link development of Gorgon with a potential expansion of the neighboring North West Shelf gas field to meet projected increases in Japanese gas demand.
On its own, development of Gorgon would cost between A$6 billion and A$10 billion, analysts have said.
A joint development with the North West Shelf could reduce the initial size of Gorgon, lowering the cost.
Chevron, which also holds a one-sixth stake in the North West Shelf consortium, told Reuters recently it was confident an agreement on joint development could be reached.
Gorgon's production capability has been projected at between 12 million and 15 million tonnes of liquified natural gas annually for 20 years.
The North West shelf currently produces about 7.3 million tonnes of LNG a year and has proposed its own expansion to some 14 million tonnes annually.
Equal partners in the North West shelf are Woodside Ltd, Broken Hill Pty Co ltd, Royal/Dutch Shell Group, British Petroleum Inc Plc, Japan (LNG) Pty Ltd (MiMi) and Chevron.
